reason: The text names two characters who are not leaders: Shiphrah (שִׁפְרָה) and Puah (פּוּעָה), identified explicitly as Hebrew midwives (מְיַלְּדֹת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּת). While the Pharaoh is named and is unambiguously a leader, the midwives are skilled professionals subordinate to royal authority, not leaders in the political or military sense. Despite their moral courage in defying Pharaoh's decree, their professional status and role make them something other than leaders.
